bull.b: CAVA is demonstrating broad-based demand growth through both restaurant expansion and stronger established-store performance. Rising traffic alongside higher revenue supports the durability of the brand proposition and provides a solid base for continued sales growth over the next several quarters.

New-unit productivity above 100% and strong average unit volumes indicate that expansion is generating attractive sales from recently opened restaurants. This supports CAVA’s ability to scale its footprint while reinforcing brand reach, future revenue capacity, and operating leverage.

bull.t: Strong Liquidity and Operating Cash Flow
bull.b: Substantial liquidity and positive operating cash flow give CAVA meaningful flexibility to fund restaurant openings, technology, labor, and other growth initiatives internally. The absence of debt outstanding in the reported quarter also reduces immediate financing pressure as the company expands.

bear.b: Profitability has improved from earlier losses, but the sharp decline from the 2024 net-margin peak shows that earnings are not yet consistently protected from cost and investment pressures. Lower normalized margins could constrain profit growth even if sales continue expanding.

bear.t: Persistent Food, Labor, and Delivery Cost Pressure
bear.b: Several major operating-cost categories are rising simultaneously, creating ongoing pressure on restaurant-level profitability. Fuel surcharges, wage investment, and delivery-related expenses may limit margin expansion and require continued pricing, productivity, or mix improvements to preserve earnings quality.

bear.t: Capital-Intensive and Variable Free Cash Flow
bear.b: Operating cash generation is strong, but a relatively small portion remains after capital spending, reflecting substantial reinvestment needs for the growth program. Historically volatile free cash flow can reduce flexibility for shareholder returns or expansion if operating conditions weaken.
